description: Curated historical Accra flood events for backtesting the ThirdWave geospatial vulnerability grid and seeding a demo of the CitizenReport -> Incident operational loop. NOT crowdsourced/live citizen data -- hindsight-curated from public news/reference sources, geocoded via OpenStreetMap Nominatim. Locations left ungeocoded where sources did not name a specific, unambiguous site rather than guessing.

events.name: Kwame Nkrumah Circle flood and fuel station explosion
events.deaths: over 200 (flood + GOIL fuel station explosion combined, per contemporary reporting)
events.cause: Heavy rainfall, choked drainage/gutters, floodwater carried petrol from a filling station which ignited

events.name: 2016 Accra floods
events.location_name: Accra (city-wide, no specific site named in source)
events.geocode_confidence: none - source does not name a specific location
events.cause: Heavy rainfall; streets flooded within 6 hours of rain

events.name: March 2023 Accra flood
events.cause: Rain-bearing cloud system over southeastern Ghana; inadequate drainage
events.note: Independent confirmation of the same Circle/Odaw corridor hotspot flooding again 8 years after the 2015 disaster.

events.name: Ashaiman flood
events.geocode_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (town centre, not exact bridge sites)
events.geocode_confidence: medium - town centre used; source names specific destroyed bridges (Valco Flat, Ashaiman Lebanon, Roman Down) not individually geocoded
events.cause: Over 12 hours of continuous heavy downpour

events.name: Weija Dam spillage flood
events.location_name: Weija, Greater Accra (also affected: Ashalaja, Oblogo, Tetegu)
events.geocode_confidence: high for Weija; Ashalaja/Oblogo could not be confidently geocoded and are not plotted
events.cause: Prolonged heavy rainfall raised Weija Dam level to 49.5ft (max operating level 48ft); Ghana Water Company opened 4 spill gates
events.note: Weija flooded again in May 2025 (see WEIJA-FLOOD-2025-05) -- recurring hotspot, same pattern as Kwame Nkrumah Circle.

events.name: May 2025 Accra storm flood
events.location_name: Weija, Greater Accra (also affected region-wide: Ofankor Barrier, Kaneshie, Labadi, Adentan-Dodowa, parts of Tema)
events.geocode_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (Weija used as anchor; other affected areas not individually geocoded -- multi-site regional event)
events.geocode_confidence: medium - regional event, Weija is one of several named affected areas

events.name: May 2026 Kaneshie flood
events.cause: Heavy downpour; also affected Kpone Barrier and Santa Maria
events.note: No casualties reported for this event -- vehicles stranded and major roads gridlocked. Kaneshie (Ablekuma Central Municipal) is inside the pilot district and floods repeatedly (see also ACCRA-FLOOD-2026-06-29).

events.name: June 2026 Accra floods
events.location_name: Kwame Nkrumah Circle, Accra (regional event -- also affected Alajo, Adabraka, Kaneshie, Weija, Tse Addo, Ofankor, Pantang, Ashongman Estates, parts of Tema)
events.geocode_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (Circle used as anchor; other named areas not individually geocoded -- multi-site regional event, see ALAJO-FLOOD-2026-06-29 for one that is)
events.geocode_confidence: medium - regional event, Circle is one of several named affected areas
events.displaced: 7,761 households (3,882 people) per Ghana News Agency; other contemporary reports cited up to 48,000 displaced
events.cause: Torrential rainfall described by officials as one of the heaviest to hit Accra in recent years
events.note: GNFS reported 150+ people rescued. Lectures/exams suspended at some tertiary institutions; GRIDCo/ECG cut power from Mallam and Achimota substations as a precaution.

events.name: Alajo electrocution deaths (June 2026 Accra floods)
events.cause: Floodwater entered homes and contacted electrical installations; part of the same June 29, 2026 storm as ACCRA-FLOOD-2026-06-29
events.note: OSM/Nominatim labels this area's district as 'Ayawaso Central Municipal', but it falls inside our own pilot_district_assemblies.geojson polygon for Ablekuma North Municipal -- used the latter (our authoritative boundary) for district assignment, consistent with how the rest of this project resolves district membership.

events.name: 2023 Akosombo/Kpong Dam spillage
events.location_name: Mepe, North Tongu District, Volta Region (also affected: Central/South Tongu, Asuogyaman District (Eastern Region), Tefle, Wume, Sokpoe; Alikekope, Agorme, Agbave reported as having 'completely disappeared')
events.geocode_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim (Mepe used as anchor -- 'most affected' per Wikipedia -- other named communities not individually geocoded)
events.geocode_confidence: medium - regional event spanning multiple districts, Mepe is one of several named affected areas
events.cause: Sustained heavy 2023 rainfall raised the Akosombo reservoir above its 276ft maximum operating level; VRA began controlled spillage at both Akosombo and Kpong dams on 2023-09-15, intensified 2023-10-09, flooding communities downstream on the Volta River
events.note: OUTSIDE both the pilot district and the 4-district extended coverage (Volta/Eastern Region, not Greater Accra) -- included as a reference dam-release event, not a location this project scores. Same hazard_type as the Weija events below; useful for the AI Assistant to recognize dam-release flooding as a distinct pattern from urban/flash flooding, even where it can't provide a zone score for the location.

events.name: May 2026 Weija Dam spillage flood
events.location_name: Tetegu, Weija Gbawe Municipal (also affected: Ashbread, Kinshasha, White Cross, Oblogo, Tatop)
events.geocode_confidence: high for Tetegu; other named communities not individually geocoded
events.displaced: hundreds of homes flooded; Regional Security Council (REGSEC) ordered evacuation of all downstream communities
events.cause: Ghana Water Limited opened all spill gates 2026-05-27 after the dam's water level exceeded 48ft. Contested cause worth keeping both sides of: GWL itself publicly attributed the resulting FLOODING (not the spillage decision) to illegal structures and waterway encroachment rather than the spillage alone -- directly consistent with this project's own channel-encroachment findings (see channel_encroachment_index.py).
events.note: Third documented Weija dam-release flood in this file (see WEIJA-DAM-FLOOD-2022-10-04, WEIJA-FLOOD-2025-05) -- a genuinely recurring hazard, not a one-off. This is the only event in this file where an official source explicitly names encroachment/illegal structures as a contributing cause rather than just 'heavy rain'.
